vendor_quote_source.title: NICT Universal Communication Research Institute: ICC-Crawler

what_en: ICC-Crawler is a crawler run by the Universal Communication Research Institute at Japan's National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT). NICT says it uses collected pages for research and development of information processing technologies, including multilingual translation, information analysis and artificial intelligence. NICT may also provide collected information or research products to third parties, to the extent permitted by law.
block_en: NICT says ICC-Crawler supports the Robots Exclusion Protocol and that adding User-agent: ICC-Crawler with Disallow: / to robots.txt could disable collection from all pages. It also lets site owners block a path or file type, or allow selected paths under a full Disallow. If access continues after that, NICT asks site owners to contact it so it can stop collecting from the host.
compare_en: Both collect pages that feed AI development, but ICC-Crawler is run by a Japanese public research institute for its own research and publishes two crawler IP addresses on its page, while GPTBot is run by a commercial company.
